failures.criterion: The server itself embeds everything it holds after boot, including items written before the embedding triggers existed, with no command run by a person (spec line 4; plan Decision 8: the coverage pass at start and every 10 minutes beside the scan loop)
failures.evidence: Run (packages/envoy/internal/dispatch/embedqueue/queue.go:76-80) marks one context with store.WithTransactionTracking and hands it to both runCoverage (its own goroutine) and the scan loop. The pool's hold mark lives in that context (store/pool.go:79-91), so while one loop has a cursor open the other loop's next statement is refused as a nested acquire; store.ForConcurrentRead's doc (pool.go:93-99) names exactly this ('Reads sharing one mark would refuse each other'). Live: booting the head's binary on Azure with 50 pending 32,000-character comments logged 'dispatch: second pooled connection requested while one is held' and 'dispatch embedqueue: coverage pass failed; the next one runs on schedule error="coverage pass: issue: this caller already holds a connection of the pool: a second one would deadlock it"' (stack: Cover coverage.go:217 <- runCoverage <- Run queue.go:78), so the pass that adds pre-trigger items, repairs stale rows and drops foreign vectors stopped and waits 10 minutes; a large production backlog keeps the scan loop's cursors open often, so passes keep failing. The reverse also holds: the pass's Coverage cursor refuses the scan loop's statements, and one loop's release clears the mark the other still needs, so the guard stops protecting either. Red test (commit f2d360158d8bee04cff0a8e158a24c6be6bf6a5e): TestRunsCoveragePassIsNotRefusedWhileTheScanLoopHoldsACursor in packages/envoy/internal/dispatch/embedqueue/coverage_test.go holds the scan loop's claim cursor open through a protocol-pausing proxy while the pass runs. azureRequestTimeout (60 s) is shorter than Azure's time for a dense batch: one direct request of 40 CJK bodies (1,049,910 tokens) took 65.0 s and succeeded.
